question.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(-\sqrt{x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
question.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & =\sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}})=\frac{2}{5\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}}} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{5\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}})=-\frac{6}{25\sqrt[5]{{x}^{8}}} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
A={\sqrt[5]{{x}^{2}},\frac{2}{5\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}}},-\frac{6}{25\sqrt[5]{{x}^{8}}},…}
$$

Consequently, $A$ is infinite.

- The set $B$ is also infinite. Similar to the previous case, listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & =-\sqrt{x} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\sqrt{x})=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})=\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{x}^{3}}} \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
B={-\sqrt{x},-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}},\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{x}^{3}}},…}
$$

Consequently, $B$ is infinite.

- The set $C$ is also infinite. Listing a few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})=-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})=\frac{6}{{x}^{4}} \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
C={\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}},\frac{6}{{x}^{4}},…}
$$

Consequently, $C$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A,$ $B,$ and $C.$"
